title: Field-valued fibre flatness agrees with the etale scheme-chart fibre test
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]; put $g=h\circ f$. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Fix $x\in|X|$. For every representative $\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with $K$ a field [def-weil-field], put $z_K=g\xi$, $X_{z_K}=X\times_{Z,z_K}\operatorname{Spec}K$, $Y_{z_K}=Y\times_{Z,z_K}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and let $F_{z_K}$ be the pullback of $F$. Let $\widetilde x$ be the point of $X_{z_K}$ defined by $(\xi,\mathrm{id})$. Relative flatness of a quasi-coherent module at a space point means that on every compatible etale scheme-chart diagram its ordinary Zariski stalk is flat over the corresponding base local ring; module flatness is [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. On a scheme chart, a small-etale quasi-coherent module is interpreted as its Zariski module by restriction to opens [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Consider any compatible scheme diagram $U\to V\to W$ with etale vertical maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, $c:W\to Z$, and any $u\in U$ mapping to $x$. Write $v\in V$ and $w\in W$ for its images and put $U_w=U\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ and $V_w=V\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $F_w$ be the ordinary quasi-coherent module on $U_w$ obtained by tensor pullback of the Zariski module of $a^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $F_{z_K}$ is flat over $Y_{z_K}$ at $\widetilde x$ if and only if $(F_w)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V_w,v}$. This holds for every such representative and diagram; such diagrams and points $u$ exist. Consequently either condition is independent of all these choices. There are no finiteness, relative-flatness, nonzero-module, or Noetherian assumptions.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to Z$, then a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to W\times_ZY$, and finally one $U\to V\times_YX$. Fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Base change and composition of etale coverings [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that the composites $V\to Y$ and $U\to X$ are etale and surjective on point classes. Thus some $u\in U$ maps to $x$. This proves existence; from now on fix ANY diagram and point allowed by the statement, not necessarily this surjective choice.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: Fix also ANY representative $\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ of $x$. The residue-field representative $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U\to X$ and $\xi$ have the same class. By the equivalence relation in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], there are a field $L$ and embeddings $K\to L$, $\kappa(u)\to L$ for which the maps to $X$ agree. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its map to $U$ induces maps to $V$ and $W$, the last factoring through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$. These maps and $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ have the same composite to $Z$.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: Put $B=V\times_WT=V_w\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)}T$, $A=U\times_WT=U_w\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)}T$, and $D=X_{z_K}\times_{Y_{z_K}}B$. These are fibre products, with $A,B$ schemes. The equality of maps in step 2 defines a point $t\in A$ lying over $u$ and over $\widetilde x\in X_{z_K}$; write $d$ for its image in $D$ and $b$ for its image in $B$. The identities $D=(X\times_YV)\times_VB$ and $A=U\times_VB$ follow by matching the projections and their equalities. Both $U\to X$ and $X\times_YV\to X$ are etale, so $U\to X\times_YV$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Its base change $A\to D$ is therefore an etale scheme chart. The square $D\to X_{z_K}$ over $B\to Y_{z_K}$ is cartesian, as is the square $A\to U_w$ over $B\to V_w$.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: Let $N$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent module on $A$ corresponding to the pullback of $F$ along $A\to X$. Pullbacks of $F$ to $X_{z_K}$ and $D$ remain quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. By [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition], pulling $F_{z_K}$ to $D$ and then to $A$ is canonically the same pullback of $F$: locally both iterated tensors map $c\otimes(e\otimes m)$ to $c\,e\otimes m$. The other path $A\to U_w\to U\to X$ gives the same module. The pullback comparison for arbitrary scheme morphisms in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies this latter module with the ordinary tensor pullback of $F_w$ along $A\to U_w$. Thus all the modules compared below are $N$, with the scalar actions from $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: The map $B\to V_w$ is the base change of the field extension $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$, hence flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat] and [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Also factor $B\to Y_{z_K}$ as $B\to V\times_ZT\to Y\times_ZT\to Y_{z_K}$. The last arrow is base change of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, hence flat. The middle arrow is base change of $V\to Y$, hence etale. The first is base change of the diagonal $W\to W\times_ZW$ along the pair of maps $V\times_ZT\to W$ furnished by $V$ and $T$; the diagonal is etale by etale permanence, since both $W\to Z$ and $W\times_ZW\to Z$ are etale. Therefore all three factors are flat and their composite is flat. The permanence statements and etale-implies-flat used here are exactly [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces (in particular to morphisms representable by algebraic spaces).

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: Apply both clauses of [lem-sfb-space-pointwise-module-flat-base-change] to the ACTUAL cartesian square $D=X_{z_K}\times_{Y_{z_K}}B$, at $d$ over $\widetilde x$. The base map $B\to Y_{z_K}$ is flat at $b$ by step 5, and the module is quasi-coherent by step 4. Consequently $F_{z_K}$ is flat over $Y_{z_K}$ at $\widetilde x$ if and only if its pullback to $D$ is flat over $B$ at $d$.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: The etale scheme chart $A\to D$ at $t$, together with the identity chart $B\to B$, is an admissible chart diagram for $D\to B$. By [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts], flatness of the pulled-back module on $D$ at $d$ is equivalent to the single condition that $N_t$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. The node states both directions, including that one such chart and point suffices; neither this chart nor $A\to D$ has to be surjective. Its quasi-coherent hypothesis holds by step 4.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: Apply both clauses of the SCHEME statement [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] to the cartesian square $A=U_w\times_{V_w}B$ at $t$ over $u$. Its base map $B\to V_w$ is flat by step 5. Step 4 identifies the pulled-back module with $N$. Thus $N_t$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$ if and only if $(F_w)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V_w,v}$. Combining this equivalence with steps 6 and 7 proves the assertion for the arbitrary representative and arbitrary diagram fixed above.

source.place: Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), including the choice-independence and diagram-existence assertions in its proof.

proof.text: For two representatives, compare each with one diagram supplied by step 1; both field-fibre tests are equivalent to the same chart-fibre test. For two diagrams, compare each with one representative of $x$; both chart-fibre tests are equivalent to the same field-fibre test. This proves independence of all choices. The argument never uses a nonzero stalk, finite presentation, relative flatness over $Z$, or a Noetherian assumption. In particular the zero module gives true flatness conditions on both sides.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-123cd60a5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 05WY in full (statement, existence paragraph, proofs of (1)-(3) and (2)-(3)), the item's nine steps and the statements of all 12 cited nodes. No new nodes, and the statement is unchanged: it is byte-identical to live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit. There is no repair note and no other node duplicating 05WY. The report's source error is real: the left square of the source's final diagram is not cartesian (counterexample with U = Spec k ⊔ Spec k). The delivery repairs it by inserting the true fibre product D = X_z ×_{Y_z} B = (X×_YV)×_VB, applying 05VW (lem-sfb-space-pointwise-module-flat-base-change, both clauses) to D, then 05VU (lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts) to the étale chart A = U×_VB → D, then 047C on the scheme square A = U_w×_{V_w}B. I checked: the common-field argument from the point-class definition; the identities for A, B, D and the point t; the étale map U→X×_YV by the permanence clause; flatness of B→V_w; flatness of B→Y_{z_K} as diagonal base change, then étale, then field base change; and the module identification through tensor composition and the Zariski–étale comparison. Small cases checked: F=0, identity charts, disconnected U, transcendental L, empty X. Batch-5 flags: all eight cited nodes are generic algebraic-space foundations (03FX/03BX, 03FT-03FV, 03BU, 03GA, 03D8, 04XC, 05VW, 05VU), not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so they are accepted. The four tool_uses (atlas, fibre products, étale permanence, Zariski–étale) are accepted. No SGA source is used. No changes.
